units.title: Level 1
units.blurb: The most familiar of the thousand: words strong readers meet often in good newspapers, textbooks and novels. Topics: Good and Bad: bene- and mal-; Kind and Cruel; Polite and Rude; Saying More or Less; Happy; Evidence and Proof; Fleeting and Lasting; Making Things Better; Agreeing and Disagreeing; Plenty and Scarcity.

units.title: Level 2
units.blurb: Still common in good prose, and very often tested: words worth knowing cold. Topics: Belief, Trust and Truth: cred, fid and ver; Honest and Dishonest; Eager and Reluctant; Words of Praise; Sad; Belief and Doubt; Changeable; Making Things Worse; Laws and Rules; Ordinary and Overused.

units.title: Level 3
units.blurb: Words that sharpen how you describe people, ideas and actions. Topics: Looking and Seeing: spec and vid; Brave and Fearful; Strict and Lenient; Words of Blame; Angry and Hateful; Noticing and Understanding; How Often; Helping Along; Who Rules; Unusual.

units.title: Level 4
units.blurb: A step up: words that show up in college reading and in the hardest test passages. Topics: Speaking and Saying: loqu and dict; Proud and Humble; Right and Wrong; Arguing a Case; Calm; Comparing and Contrasting; Beginnings; Getting in the Way; Guilt and Innocence; Big and Small.

units.title: Level 5
units.blurb: The middle of the climb, including twins that trip up even careful readers. Topics: Turning, Throwing and Pulling: vert, ject and tract; Careful and Careless; Real and Fake; Tricky Twins; Fear and Worry; Learners and Experts; Peaks and Endings; Calming Things Down; Fighting and Making Peace; Everywhere.

units.title: Level 6
units.blurb: Words for subtler shades of meaning. Topics: Words of Time: chron, temp and ann; Friendly and Aloof; Models and Examples; Clear and Unclear; Puzzled; Dreamers and Doers; Growing and Shrinking; Stirring Things Up; Giving In; Important and Trivial.

units.title: Level 7
units.blurb: Less common words that make writing precise. Topics: Not: in-, im- and ir-; Stubborn and Yielding; Self-Control and Indulgence; Joking and Mocking; Bored and Interested; Strong and Weak Arguments; Before and After; Stopping and Holding Back; Judging Fairly; Hard and Easy.

units.title: Level 8
units.blurb: Rarer words, often from Latin and Greek, that reward knowing their roots. Topics: Feeling, Loving and Humankind: path, phil and anthrop; Wise and Foolish; Insults and Slights; Loud and Angry Words; Lazy and Sleepy; Inborn and Acquired; Waiting and Hurrying; Coaxing and Forcing; Insiders and Outsiders; Too Much.

units.title: Level 9
units.blurb: Uncommon words for strong readers, including words whose meanings are not what they seem. Topics: Flocks, Peace and Pleasing: greg, pac and plac; Spenders and Savers; Tricks and Schemes; Slippery Speech; Regret and Shame; Obvious and Seeming; Luck and Chance; Destroying; Secret and Hidden; Showy and Plain.

units.title: Level 10
units.blurb: The rarest of the thousand: words for the strongest readers and writers. Topics: All, Both, Good and Over: omni, pan, ambi, eu and hyper; Flatterers and the Bold; Leanings and Likings; Rare Words for Praise and Blame; Not What They Seem; Deep and Shallow Thinking; Old and New; Taking and Giving Up; Rebels and Factions; Harmful and Wholesome.

topics.title: Good and Bad: bene- and mal-
topics.short: bene- means well and mal- means badly: two small parts that unlock a family of words.
topics.trouble: Learners mix up benefactor (the giver) and beneficiary (the receiver), and take malign for an adjective only; it is most often a verb: to speak ill of someone.

topics.title: Kind and Cruel
topics.short: Words for warm hearts and cold ones.
topics.trouble: humane (kind) is not human; callous (unfeeling) is not callus (hard skin). magnanimous is about a big heart, not a big size.

topics.title: Polite and Rude
topics.short: Words for good manners and bad ones.
topics.trouble: discreet (careful, private) is not discrete (separate). brusque and curt are about too few words, not loud ones.

topics.title: Saying More or Less
topics.short: Words for people of few words and people of many.
topics.trouble: laconic and taciturn are close: a laconic person speaks briefly; a taciturn person seldom speaks at all. succinct is pronounced suk-SINKT.

topics.title: Happy
topics.short: Words for joy, cheer and hope.
topics.trouble: blithe can be a criticism: a blithe disregard for danger is carelessness. sanguine comes from the Latin for blood, but in English it means hopeful.

topics.title: Evidence and Proof
topics.short: Words for testing ideas and backing them up.
topics.trouble: anecdotal evidence is real stories, but too few or too unrepresentative to prove a pattern. extrapolate reaches beyond the data; interpolate fills in between data points.

topics.title: Fleeting and Lasting
topics.short: Words for what passes quickly and what lasts.
topics.trouble: ephemeral things don't last, but that does not make them unimportant. indelible ink cannot be erased; an indelible memory cannot be forgotten.

topics.title: Making Things Better
topics.short: Words for improving, easing and fixing.
topics.trouble: mitigate (lessen) is often confused with militate (to work against: "militate against"). ameliorate improves a bad situation; it is not used for making a good thing better.

topics.title: Agreeing and Disagreeing
topics.short: Words for coming together and pulling apart.
topics.trouble: consensus means general agreement, so "general consensus" says it twice. dissent (disagreement) is not descent (going down).

topics.title: Plenty and Scarcity
topics.short: Words for having lots, and for having little.
topics.trouble: plethora first meant too many; today it often means a great many. myriad can be an adjective (myriad stars) or a noun (a myriad of stars).

topics.title: Belief, Trust and Truth: cred, fid and ver
topics.short: cred means believe, fid means trust and ver means true.
topics.trouble: A story is incredible (hard to believe); the listener is incredulous (not believing). Credulous means too ready to believe, the opposite of incredulous. A confidant (a trusted friend) is not confident (sure of yourself).

topics.title: Honest and Dishonest
topics.short: Words for telling the truth and for bending it.
topics.trouble: disingenuous is not the opposite of ingenious; it means insincere, often pretending innocence. candid means open and honest, as in a candid answer or a candid (unposed) photo.

topics.title: Eager and Reluctant
topics.short: Words for wanting to do something, and for not wanting to.
topics.trouble: loath (unwilling, an adjective) is not loathe (to hate, a verb). averse (unwilling) is not adverse (harmful).

topics.title: Words of Praise
topics.short: Words for speaking well of someone.
topics.trouble: exalt (praise, raise up) is not exult (rejoice). adulation goes beyond admiration toward flattery.

topics.title: Sad
topics.short: Words for sorrow, gloom and longing.
topics.trouble: poignant is pronounced POIN-yunt; it can describe a tender memory as well as a sad one. morose suggests sullen bad temper, not only sadness.

topics.title: Belief and Doubt
topics.short: Words for believing, supposing and doubting.
topics.trouble: tenet (a principle) is not tenant (a renter). skeptical is doubt about claims; cynical is distrust of people's motives.

topics.title: Changeable
topics.short: Words for people and things that change without warning.
topics.trouble: spontaneous is often good (a spontaneous smile); impetuous and impulsive usually warn. vacillate is about indecision; fluctuate is about changing amounts.

topics.title: Making Things Worse
topics.short: Words for weakening, damaging and worsening.
topics.trouble: compound as a verb means to make worse (compound an error), not only to combine. aggravate in careful use means to make worse; "to annoy" is a common everyday meaning.

topics.title: Laws and Rules
topics.short: Words for making rules and unmaking them.
topics.trouble: statute (a law) is not statue (a sculpture) or stature (height or standing). ratify approves; repeal and rescind undo.

topics.title: Ordinary and Overused
topics.short: Words for the everyday and the worn out.
topics.trouble: pedestrian as an adjective means dull, not "on foot." mundane means ordinary, not bad.

topics.title: Looking and Seeing: spec and vid
topics.short: spec, spic and vid, vis mean look and see.
topics.trouble: specious sounds like "special" or "spacious" but means falsely convincing. perspicacious (sharp-minded) describes a person; perspicuous (clearly expressed) describes writing.

topics.title: Brave and Fearful
topics.short: Words for courage and for its lack.
topics.trouble: audacious can praise boldness or criticize rudeness; read the context. intrepid has nothing to do with trips: it comes from in- (not) and trepidus (alarmed).

topics.title: Strict and Lenient
topics.short: Words for firm rules and loose ones.
topics.trouble: rigorous praises thoroughness; draconian criticizes harshness. lax is about loose rules; lenient is about mercy toward someone.

topics.title: Words of Blame
topics.short: Words for speaking against someone.
topics.trouble: censure (formal blame) is not censor (to remove material). admonish is the gentlest word here; berate is among the harshest.

topics.title: Angry and Hateful
topics.short: Words for anger, from annoyance to hatred.
topics.trouble: indignant anger is about unfairness, not about any annoyance. livid first meant bluish, like a bruise; in everyday use it means furious.

topics.title: Noticing and Understanding
topics.short: Words for paying attention and taking things in.
topics.trouble: wary (cautious) is not weary (tired). oblivious is followed by "to" or "of": oblivious to the noise.

topics.title: How Often
topics.short: Words for now and then, again and again, and without end.
topics.trouble: continual means repeated with breaks; continuous means without a break. A dripping faucet is continual; a flowing river is continuous.

topics.title: Helping Along
topics.short: Words for making things easier and helping them grow.
topics.trouble: abet usually means helping wrongdoing (to aid and abet). galvanize means to jolt into action, not just to coat with zinc.

topics.title: Who Rules
topics.short: Words for kinds of power and government.
topics.trouble: anarchy means "without a ruler"; in everyday use it means chaos. oligarchy (rule by a few) is not monarchy (rule by one).

topics.title: Unusual
topics.short: Words for the odd, the out of place and the never seen before.
topics.trouble: bizarre (strange) is not bazaar (a market). unprecedented means never happened before, not merely rare.

topics.title: Speaking and Saying: loqu and dict
topics.short: loqu and locut mean speak; dict means say.
topics.trouble: indict is pronounced in-DITE: the c is silent. A soliloquy is spoken alone on stage; a monologue may be spoken to others.

topics.title: Proud and Humble
topics.short: Words for people who think too much of themselves, and for those who don't.
topics.trouble: hubris is more than pride: it is pride that leads to a fall. supercilious comes from the Latin word for eyebrow (raised in scorn), not from "silly."

topics.title: Right and Wrong
topics.short: Words for honorable conduct and dishonorable conduct.
topics.trouble: venal (open to bribes) is not venial (minor and easily forgiven). propriety (proper conduct) is not proprietary (owned).

topics.title: Arguing a Case
topics.short: Words for making a claim and answering one.
topics.trouble: refute means to prove wrong, not just to deny; rebut means to argue against, whether or not you win.

topics.title: Calm
topics.short: Words for peace of mind and steady nerves.
topics.trouble: impassive (showing no feeling) is not impassioned (full of feeling); they are opposites. nonchalant can mean calm or too unconcerned.

topics.title: Comparing and Contrasting
topics.short: Words for likeness and difference.
topics.trouble: A dichotomy is a split into two opposites; using it for any difference stretches it. disparate means fundamentally unlike, not just different.

topics.title: Beginnings
topics.short: Words for starting, and for things just begun.
topics.trouble: nascent and incipient are close; incipient often warns of something unwelcome (an incipient problem). fledgling comes from a young bird learning to fly.

topics.title: Getting in the Way
topics.short: Words for slowing things down and blocking them.
topics.trouble: preclude rules something out ahead of time; it is stronger than hinder. forestall means acting early to prevent, like stepping in front of a problem.

topics.title: Guilt and Innocence
topics.short: Words for blame, punishment and pardon.
topics.trouble: condone means to allow or overlook, not to condemn; they are near opposites. vindicate means to clear or prove right; it has nothing to do with revenge (vindictive).

topics.title: Big and Small
topics.short: Words for the enormous and the tiny.
topics.trouble: minuscule is spelled with a u (from minus), not "miniscule." minute the adjective is pronounced my-NOOT.

topics.title: Turning, Throwing and Pulling: vert, ject and tract
topics.short: vert means turn, ject means throw and tract means pull.
topics.trouble: adverse (harmful: adverse effects) is not averse (unwilling: averse to risk). inadvertent means accidental, not careless on purpose.

topics.title: Careful and Careless
topics.short: Words for doing things with great care, and with too little.
topics.trouble: scrupulous can mean careful about details or careful about right and wrong. cursory (hasty) has nothing to do with cursing: it comes from Latin for running.

topics.title: Real and Fake
topics.short: Words for the real thing and for imitations.
topics.trouble: apocryphal stories are doubtful, not proven false. veritable stresses that a description fits (a veritable feast); it does not mean "literally."

topics.title: Tricky Twins
topics.short: Pairs of words that look or sound alike but mean different things.
topics.trouble: Speakers imply; listeners infer. affect is usually the verb and effect the noun (though effect can be a verb meaning "to bring about"). ingenuous (innocent) and ingenious (clever) differ by one letter.

topics.title: Fear and Worry
topics.short: Words for fear, from a twinge of doubt to dread.
topics.trouble: daunt (discourage) and taunt (mock) sound alike. A qualm is a twinge of doubt or conscience, not a full fear.

topics.title: Learners and Experts
topics.short: Words for beginners, dabblers and masters.
topics.trouble: pedantic is a criticism; erudite is praise. precocious can praise a child's early skill or criticize a child for acting too old.

topics.title: Peaks and Endings
topics.short: Words for high points, low points and endings.
topics.trouble: zenith and nadir are opposites: the highest and the lowest point. culminate means to reach a climax, not simply to end.

topics.title: Calming Things Down
topics.short: Words for soothing feelings and settling quarrels.
topics.trouble: defuse (calm a situation, as if removing a bomb's fuse) is not diffuse (spread out). You allay fears; you don't "alley" or "ally" them.

topics.title: Fighting and Making Peace
topics.short: Words for conflict and for ending it.
topics.trouble: belligerent and bellicose share bellum (war): bellicose describes a temperament, belligerent a behavior. A truce is a pause; an armistice ends the fighting of a war.

topics.title: Everywhere
topics.short: Words for what is found all around.
topics.trouble: endemic (always present in one place) differs from epidemic (a sudden spread). diffuse (spread out) is not defuse (calm a situation).

topics.title: Words of Time: chron, temp and ann
topics.short: chron (Greek) and temp (Latin) mean time; ann and enn mean year.
topics.trouble: chronic means long-lasting or recurring, not "severe." contemporary can mean "of the same time as" (a contemporary of the author) or "modern"; context decides.

topics.title: Friendly and Aloof
topics.short: Words for warm company and for keeping apart.
topics.trouble: reticent means reluctant to speak or share, not reluctant in general. amiable describes people; amicable describes relationships and agreements.

topics.title: Models and Examples
topics.short: Words for the best examples and the patterns others follow.
topics.trouble: epitome is pronounced ih-PIT-uh-mee. emulate means imitating out of admiration, hoping to match or surpass, not just copying.

topics.title: Clear and Unclear
topics.short: Words for ideas that are easy to follow and ideas that are not.
topics.trouble: implicit means unstated, not "hidden on purpose"; explicit and implicit are opposites. obscure has two meanings: hard to understand, and little known.

topics.title: Puzzled
topics.short: Words for being confused, and for the puzzles that confuse us.
topics.trouble: A dilemma is a hard choice between two options, not any problem. A quandary is the uncertain state you are in; a conundrum is the puzzle itself.

topics.title: Dreamers and Doers
topics.short: Words for big dreams and practical plans.
topics.trouble: quixotic comes from the hero of a famous novel who attacked windmills, thinking they were giants; it means admirably but impractically idealistic. feasible means doable, not "likely."

topics.title: Growing and Shrinking
topics.short: Words for growth and decline.
topics.trouble: The moon waxes and wanes: wane means shrink. abate is used for storms, noise and pain that ease.

topics.title: Stirring Things Up
topics.short: Words for starting trouble and spurring action.
topics.trouble: foment (stir up trouble) is not ferment, though both suggest bubbling. incite (urge on) is not insight (understanding).

topics.title: Giving In
topics.short: Words for yielding, surrendering and agreeing to go along.
topics.trouble: accede (agree) is not exceed (go beyond). acquiesce means quiet acceptance, not eager agreement.

topics.title: Important and Trivial
topics.short: Words for what matters most and what hardly matters.
topics.trouble: salient means standing out, not salty. A tangential remark touches the topic and then goes off in another direction.

topics.title: Not: in-, im- and ir-
topics.short: The prefix in- often means not, and changes to im- or ir- to fit the next sound.
topics.trouble: Not every in- means not: inflammable means easily set on fire, and invaluable means priceless. The in- that means not becomes im- before b, m and p, il- before l and ir- before r.

topics.title: Stubborn and Yielding
topics.short: Words for holding firm and for giving way.
topics.trouble: tenacious and steadfast usually praise; obstinate and recalcitrant usually blame. The same firmness gets a kind word or an unkind one depending on the writer's view.

topics.title: Self-Control and Indulgence
topics.short: Words for holding back and for giving in to pleasure.
topics.trouble: ascetic (self-denying) is not aesthetic (about beauty). epicurean today means fond of fine food, though the ancient philosopher it is named for taught simple pleasures.

topics.title: Joking and Mocking
topics.short: Words for humor, gentle and sharp.
topics.trouble: sarcastic and sardonic both mock: sarcasm says the opposite of what it means, while sardonic humor is grim. A parody imitates something; a satire need not.

topics.title: Bored and Interested
topics.short: Words for dull hours and fascinating ones.
topics.trouble: You pique interest (stir it), not "peak" or "peek" it. indifferent can mean uninterested or merely ordinary (an indifferent cook).

topics.title: Strong and Weak Arguments
topics.short: Words for arguments that hold up and arguments that fall apart.
topics.trouble: moot has two senses: open to debate (a moot point) and, in common American use, no longer mattering. In logic, valid describes reasoning that holds, whether or not its premises are true.

topics.title: Before and After
topics.short: Words for what comes first and what follows.
topics.trouble: posthumous is pronounced POS-chuh-mus: the h is silent. prescient means foreseeing; it has nothing to do with "present."

topics.title: Stopping and Holding Back
topics.short: Words for discouraging, limiting and stopping.
topics.trouble: dissuade is the opposite of persuade. stanch (stop a flow) is also spelled staunch, which also means loyal.

topics.title: Judging Fairly
topics.short: Words for fair judgment and for bias.
topics.trouble: disinterested means impartial (having nothing to gain), not uninterested (bored). A disinterested judge is a good thing.

topics.title: Hard and Easy
topics.short: Words for tasks that are hard, risky, useless or too easy.
topics.trouble: facile is usually a criticism (a facile answer), not praise. onerous means burdensome; it has nothing to do with honor.

topics.title: Feeling, Loving and Humankind: path, phil and anthrop
topics.short: path means feeling, phil means love and anthrop means human being.
topics.trouble: empathy (feeling with someone) is not sympathy (feeling sorry for someone). apathy (not caring) is not antipathy (active dislike).

topics.title: Wise and Foolish
topics.short: Words for good sense and for the lack of it.
topics.trouble: judicious means wise in judgment, not "quick to judge others." obtuse (slow to understand) also names an angle over 90 degrees.

topics.title: Insults and Slights
topics.short: Words for putting people down.
topics.trouble: deprecate (disapprove) is often confused with depreciate (lose value). A slight can be quiet: leaving someone out on purpose is a slight even if nothing is said.

topics.title: Loud and Angry Words
topics.short: Words for noise and for heated speech.
topics.trouble: vociferous is about loud expression of opinion; it does not mean wordy. cacophony is harsh noise; euphony is its pleasant opposite.

topics.title: Lazy and Sleepy
topics.short: Words for low energy, from lazy to fast asleep.
topics.trouble: soporific describes what causes sleep (a soporific lecture); somnolent describes the sleepy person. A dormant volcano can wake up again.

topics.title: Inborn and Acquired
topics.short: Words for what we are born with and what we pick up.
topics.trouble: inveterate (a long-held habit) is not invertebrate (an animal without a backbone). Intrinsic motivation comes from within; extrinsic motivation comes from rewards outside.

topics.title: Waiting and Hurrying
topics.short: Words for delays, pauses and haste.
topics.trouble: defer has two meanings: to postpone, and to yield respectfully (defer to an expert). precipitate as an adjective means hasty; as a verb it means to cause suddenly.

topics.title: Coaxing and Forcing
topics.short: Words for getting people to do things, gently or roughly.
topics.trouble: beguile can mean charm or deceive; read the context. coerce uses pressure or threats; compel can be neutral (the law compels drivers to stop at red lights).

topics.title: Insiders and Outsiders
topics.short: Words for shutting people out and for narrow or wide horizons.
topics.trouble: parochial in this sense means narrow-minded; it can also simply mean "of a parish," as in a parochial school. insular comes from the Latin for island.

topics.title: Too Much
topics.short: Words for more than enough.
topics.trouble: gratuitous means unnecessary as well as free of charge. redundant also means repeating: "free gift" is redundant.

topics.title: Flocks, Peace and Pleasing: greg, pac and plac
topics.short: greg means flock; pac means peace and plac means please.
topics.trouble: egregious once meant "standing out from the flock" in a good way; today it means shockingly bad. complacent (smug) is not complaisant (eager to please).

topics.title: Spenders and Savers
topics.short: Words for how people handle money.
topics.trouble: frugal is a compliment; parsimonious is a criticism. prodigal means wasteful, not "returning home," though a famous story about a prodigal son who came home made many people think so.

topics.title: Tricks and Schemes
topics.short: Words for tricksters and their plots.
topics.trouble: machination is pronounced mak-uh-NAY-shun, with a hard k. collusion is secret cooperation; a collision is a crash.

topics.title: Slippery Speech
topics.short: Words for dodging, hinting and misleading.
topics.trouble: dissemble (hide one's motives) is not disassemble (take apart). equivocate and prevaricate both dodge the truth; prevaricate leans toward lying.

topics.title: Regret and Shame
topics.short: Words for being sorry and for being embarrassed.
topics.trouble: chagrin mixes embarrassment with annoyance. "Without compunction" means without any guilt.

topics.title: Obvious and Seeming
topics.short: Words for what is plain to see and what only appears so.
topics.trouble: flagrant (shockingly obvious) is not fragrant. ostensible means "apparent, but maybe not real": the ostensible reason may hide the real one.

topics.title: Luck and Chance
topics.short: Words for good luck, bad luck and pure chance.
topics.trouble: fortuitous first meant "by chance," good or bad; today it is often used to mean lucky. hapless means unlucky, not helpless.

topics.title: Destroying
topics.short: Words for tearing down and wiping out.
topics.trouble: decimate once meant destroying one in ten; today it means destroying a large part, not all. raze (tear down) sounds like raise (build up).

topics.title: Secret and Hidden
topics.short: Words for secrets, stealth and things out of sight.
topics.trouble: covert (secret) and overt (open) are opposites. elusive (hard to catch) is not illusive (unreal).

topics.title: Showy and Plain
topics.short: Words for beauty, show and plainness.
topics.trouble: aesthetic (about beauty) is not ascetic (self-denying). gaudy and garish always criticize; ornate and opulent can praise.

topics.title: All, Both, Good and Over: omni, pan, ambi, eu and hyper
topics.short: omni and pan mean all, ambi means both, eu means good and hyper means over.
topics.trouble: ambivalent means pulled two ways at once, not "indifferent." hyperbole is pronounced hy-PER-buh-lee, and a eulogy (praise) is not an elegy (a sad poem).

topics.title: Flatterers and the Bold
topics.short: Words for bowing too low and for standing too tall.
topics.trouble: deferential is polite; obsequious is too much. temerity (nerve) is not timidity (shyness): they are nearly opposites.

topics.title: Leanings and Likings
topics.short: Words for what people tend toward and what they like.
topics.trouble: proclivity often hints at a bad habit; penchant and predilection are usually neutral or fond. wont (a habit) rhymes with "want" in most American speech but is a different word.

topics.title: Rare Words for Praise and Blame
topics.short: Rarer, stronger words for praising and scolding.
topics.trouble: impugn attacks someone's honesty or a claim's truth; it does not mean to punish. paean is pronounced PEE-un, like "peon," but means a song of praise.

topics.title: Not What They Seem
topics.short: Words whose meanings are not what their sound suggests.
topics.trouble: enervate means to weaken, not to energize. bemused means puzzled, not amused. noisome means smelly or harmful, not noisy. restive means restless, not restful. inflammable means flammable, not fireproof. In careful writing nonplussed means puzzled; a newer, informal American use means unbothered, so read it with care.

topics.title: Deep and Shallow Thinking
topics.short: Words for deep thought and for knowledge few people share.
topics.trouble: ruminate also describes a cow chewing its cud, so to ruminate is to chew over a thought. esoteric means for insiders, not "strange" in general.

topics.title: Old and New
topics.short: Words for the very old and the brand new.
topics.trouble: pristine means unspoiled, not just clean. hoary can describe gray hair or an idea worn out by long use (a hoary joke); antiquated and antediluvian poke fun at the old.

topics.title: Taking and Giving Up
topics.short: Words for seizing things and for letting them go.
topics.trouble: appropriate as a verb (uh-PRO-pree-ate) means to take; as an adjective (uh-PRO-pree-it) it means suitable.

topics.title: Rebels and Factions
topics.short: Words for those who break from the group, and for groups that split.
topics.trouble: maverick and iconoclast can be praise; renegade and insurgent usually are not. partisan means taking one side; bipartisan means involving both major parties.

topics.title: Harmful and Wholesome
topics.short: Words for what harms and what does good.
topics.trouble: salutary (beneficial) has nothing to do with saluting; salubrious means healthful. noxious fumes harm; obnoxious people annoy.
